A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SymbolicDet research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and complete supplementary materials support comparison despite pagination and notation changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original event-recognition experiments in Tables 1–3 and component, LLM-guidance, and search-scale analyses in the supplement.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds neuro-symbolic comparisons, USED evaluations, and computational measurements in Tables 4–7.

M1.justification: The detector-based inputs, evolutionary symbolic search, structured prompts, LLM feedback, optimization objective, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Symbol renaming and additional experiments do not establish a changed algorithm or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Section 7 and Table 7 add evaluation on USED's SPORT, CONCERT, and PROTEST subsets, extending social-event coverage, including concerts. The existing ERA, Helmet-Mac, Multi-rods Fishing, and UCSD Ped2 evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Table 4 introduces an evaluated neuro-symbolic comparator family—NSCL, NS-VQA, and LogicHOI—on both fishing and helmet benchmarks, substantially broadening comparison with reasoning-based alternatives. Table 7 also adds a comparator labelled USED, although its implementation is unspecified. Existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New comparisons are labelled Acc in Tables 4 and 7. Tables 5–6 introduce runtime per 500 iterations, time to equal performance, and component-level runtime and memory measurements. Existing splits, detection thresholds, and the stated 5,000-iteration search budget remain unchanged; the new experiments' detailed protocols are sparse.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 add computational analyses comparing no LLM with different LLM sizes and separating detector, search, and LLM overhead. These extend the earlier convergence analysis to measured resource costs. Existing component ablations, search-scale analysis, and sports illustration are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for these experiments. The new runtime and memory ranges are not identified as statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The empirical record expands through neuro-symbolic comparisons, USED results, and resource measurements. Table 4 reports fishing scores of 0.75/0.65/0.61/0.67 for Ours/NSCL/NS-VQA/LogicHOI. Table 7 reports 0.93/0.99/0.92 versus USED's 0.66/0.75/0.67. Table 5 reports 80.66 versus 267 seconds per 500 iterations without an LLM versus 72B, but 69.66 versus 26.07 seconds to equal performance. Original Tables 1–3 and plotted results remain unchanged; these are added results, not demonstrated improvements over v3 under identical settings.

T1.justification: v3 Eq. (5) applies every feature function to the same entity set E. v4 Eq. (4) instead writes phi_1(D_1), phi_2(D_2), ..., phi_d(D_n), mixing feature indices with image-specific detection sets. This is a limited, non-equivalent change to the displayed definition, without an explained procedural change. Other mathematics is largely renamed; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free, detector-agnostic event understanding through interpretable LLM-guided symbolic search, competitive performance, and contributed datasets. The additional evaluations support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly qualifies computational-cost reporting by explaining that LLM reasoning uses a third-party service and its cost can vary substantially by provider. It also introduces an explicit computational-cost versus performance discussion. Earlier mechanism explanations and applicability claims remain.

D1.justification: The abstract's code hyperlink changes from an anonymous status page to the named MAC-AutoML/SymbolicDet GitHub repository. v4 newly discloses third-party LLM hosting and measured runtime and memory requirements. Existing hardware and search hyperparameters remain; the dataset footnote still promises future availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for USED, neural-logic interaction detection, DetGPT, Groundhog, and three prompt-optimization works, while removing the GPT-4V exploration reference and example. Section 2.2 now distinguishes guiding an external symbolic search from optimizing LLM inputs. These are localized refinements to the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Changes include localized wording corrections, revised notation, correction of the architecture reference from Figure 5 to Figure 2, new appendix Sections 7–8, acknowledgments, and author-order, affiliation, and contribution-footnote edits.

P2.justification: The supplement substantially expands its displays with comparative-performance, resource-cost, and notation tables (Tables 4–8). Existing figures remain, with Figure 5 relocated above the notation table. Caption changes introduce errors: Table 3 now mentions USED despite retaining only its earlier results, and Table 7 incorrectly describes computational overhead.

improvement.justification: v4 improves coverage of relevant competing methods and practical computational costs through Tables 4–7, while preserving the original evidence and supplying a named code-repository link. The gains are limited by missing baseline-transfer and evaluation details, an unspecified equal-performance target, misleading table captions, and inconsistent revised feature notation. These additions provide useful empirical and practical information, but their documentation limits the overall improvement.
